confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for prices. They covered Victoria Falls and Zimbabwe cost-of-living aggregators, budget guides and one hotel spa-café rate page. I found no Numbeo page for Victoria Falls itself. Sources disagree: a local lager was about $3 in one guide and about $4.95 in another, and the national average is about $1.50. A cappuccino ranged from $3 to $6, and an inexpensive meal was about $10. I treated Victoria Falls as a dollarised tourist town priced above the Zimbabwe averages. The mid-range two-person meal rests on about $45-50 from CityCost-style figures and on $15-35 mains reported for tourist restaurants. Wine rests on the single undated $6-8 hotel spa-café glass price. I found no reliable cocktail price, so I set it at roughly twice the beer price, near the top of the wine range. All four accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages or listings. Low-season and high-season rates can differ a lot.
comparable_city_reasoning: Victoria Falls is a small, heavily tourist-oriented, USD-priced town. I priced it above Harare and Zimbabwe-wide averages and close to the Livingstone, Zambia tourist strip and other safari-gateway towns in southern Africa.
